card.name: Punctuation after British and French place names
card.fires_on: The comma, bracket or small linking word right after a town or place name, where a county, region or country usually comes next. Mostly in biographical or geographic text about places in England and France.

modes.label: Comma after a town
modes.description: A comma directly after a place name in a birth, death or address line, before the county or country.
modes.example: Thomas Whieldon (born September 1719 in Penkhull<<,>> Stoke-on-Trent - died March

modes.label: Link word before a place
modes.description: A small word such as in or from sitting before or after a place name in a geographic phrase.
modes.example: Landes is also the name of a commune in the Charente-Maritime département,<< in>> France.

modes.label: Bracket after a town list
modes.description: An opening bracket after a town name in a list of places with codes.

card.plain: It fires on the comma or small word after a place name, just before the county or country is given.
